column15: Verified via producer's own site: Beverbach is the single malt of Hardenberg Distillery (Hardenberg-Wilthen AG), Noerten-Hardenberg, Germany; pot-still double distillation, locally-sourced barley. Corrected kind blend->distillery: every sample (Craftbeer/Mizunara/Sherry/Tequila/Tri Cask) is a cask finish of the same single malt, not a blend. No peat mentioned across any expression on the official site; kept unknown rather than none since an unconfirmed retailer note mentioned a faint smoke character the producer's own copy never corroborates.

Confirmed via official product page: Breckenridge Distillery, Breckenridge CO, high-rye bourbon (56% corn/38% rye/6% malted barley) aged in charred new American oak. Range (Blend, Distiller's High Proof, Port/PX/Rum cask finishes) is bourbon-based throughout; no peat mentioned, consistent with standard US bourbon kilning (no peat).

Confirmed via Wikipedia and 88bamboo.co (both re-fetched this session): Chichibu distillery, Saitama Prefecture, Japan, operated by Venture Whisky Ltd; single malt. 88bamboo.co: a quarter of the malt is peated (~45ppm, Ardbeg-level), three-quarters unpeated, and releases often vat both together. No reliable per-bottling signal from names alone (On The Way, Paris Edition, Red Wine Cask), so peat stays unknown rather than guessed.

Re-confirmed all three producer pages this session: Douglas Laing's Regional Malts range (Single Grain/Single Malt/Blended Scotch across the series). Highland and Speyside editions state no peat and read as ordinary unpeated malt (honey/oak/toffee/berries) -- baseline set none. The Islay edition's own page (same domain) doesn't itself state a peat level either, but see rule.tsv: multiple independent retailers sell an explicitly heavily-peated Clan Denny Islay SKU sourced from Ardbeg/Bowmore/Bruichladdich/Bunnahabhain/Caol Ila, so the Islay-pattern rule sets heavy, corroborated by the SKU itself being Islay-sourced per Douglas Laing's own page.

Corrected: this is an Italian-produced blended whiskey, not the seed's guessed American style. Retailer product spec (Tavria V/Zakaz.ua) states country of origin Italy, manufacturer Polini Produzioni Srl, classified "blended" whiskey (mixture of grain whiskey and bourbon whiskey, prepared water, caramel E150a). No malt whisky component and no peat mentioned; ingredients support unpeated.

column7: The Vintage Malt Whisky Co. Ltd
column15: Resolved (the seed's session hit a search-budget wall): bottled by The Vintage Malt Whisky Co Ltd (founded 1992 by Brian Cook) from an undisclosed Islay distillery ("anonymous single malt"/"mystery malt"), named for Loch Finlaggan. Batch Strength measured ~40ppm; every core expression (Old Reserve/'Original Peaty', Eilean Mor, Cask Strength) is consistently reviewed peated/smoky, so set heavy for the whole line rather than per-SKU. Corroborated by region=islay (the entire range is Islay malt).

Resolved (seed's session had exhausted its search budget): Fuyu is a blended Japanese whisky (malt+grain, "Japanese blending tradition"), 40% ABV. Corrected countryCode XX->JP. No peat mentioned; tasting profile (honey, vanilla, light fruit, caramel) reads unpeated but nothing states it outright, so left unknown. Bottler not confirmed by an openable source this session (masterofmalt.com, bbcspirits.com, distiller.com all 403'd); other search results point to BBC Spirits, a Bordeaux merchant sourcing 3 Honshu distilleries -- left owner empty pending a reviewer with better access.

Confirmed via retailer product page: blended Scotch, Speyside malts as a core component plus grain whisky, no peat mentioned. Bottler/producer not identified by any source found (sold via a Jordanian retailer among others); ordinary own-label export blend.

Resolved (seed found nothing): owned/distributed by Slaur International, a French spirits wholesaler (Le Havre), sold in 70+ countries. Range spans 3/5/12-year blends, a 12-year blended malt, a 12-year single malt and a distinct NAS peated blend -- defaultTypeName stays empty. General profile is described as "light and fruity...with sweet vanilla and traces of peat", which could describe the whole range or just be conflated with the separately-named peated SKU, and isn't from Slaur's own domain, so kept unknown rather than guessed; flag for a reviewer able to pin the catalogue's bare "Glen Scanlan" sample to one specific listed SKU. Confirms the seed's cross-reference to a "Slaur Sardet Glen Scanlan" sample (same distributor).

Corrected peatProfile none->unknown: retailer product page (blended Scotch imported from Scotland, Highlands+Speyside malt and grain, 3-year, IWSC/SF World Spirits Silver medals) explicitly describes the nose/palate/finish with "malted barley toasted with peat", "slightly smoky aromas" and "a taste of dry peat" three separate times -- contradicts a flat unpeated assumption. Not a producer-domain statement though, so withheld peat proposal: light, per jensensliquors.com. Producer/bottler not identified.

Resolved (seed found nothing): produced at Loch Lomond distillery (Loch Lomond Group) -- set owner and parentSlug=loch-lomond (an existing live producer) accordingly; product names are literally "Glenshiel Highland Blended"/"Glenshiel Deluxe Highland Blended", hence region/legalRegion=highland. Malt+grain matured in American oak, no peat mentioned; kept none as an ordinary export blend, though Loch Lomond's own single malt range does include peated expressions, so flag for reviewer if a specifically peated Glenshiel SKU ever surfaces.

Resolved: owned by MacDuff International (acquired from Allied Lyons, 1992); one of the original peaty blends, created by Ian Hunter (Laphroaig's former owner), traces to Islay House in the 1920s, "the only blended whisky which can include 'Islay' in its name". Producer's own site (islaymist.com): Original is "an elegant, multi-layered scotch with balanced smoke character" and Double Peated is "twice as smoky as the Islay Mist Original" -- set peatProfile=medium for the line (Original/Deluxe/Original Peated Blend read as the same core product), corroborated on the producer's own domain. Filled defaultTypeName=blend (every expression is Blended Scotch Whisky).

Corrected kind blend->distillery: Milam & Greene runs its own copper pot stills in Blanco, TX (plus Kentucky column-still production), founded by Marsha Milam, Heather Greene and Marlene Holmes -- an operating distillery, not merely a blend. Bourbon/rye/blend range so defaultTypeName stays empty; no peat mentioned anywhere, consistent with standard American whiskey (kept none).

Resolved (seed found nothing): O'Neill's Blended Irish Whiskey is a West Cork Distillers label (Skibbereen, West Cork, Ireland; "west-cork" is an existing live producer, set as parentSlug). Sherry-cask-influenced, sweet/honeyed profile; no peat mentioned, consistent with ordinary Irish blend convention.

Confirmed: sold by Irish Distillers/Pernod Ricard to Sazerac in 2016 (re-verified via Wikipedia and scotchwhisky.com's Whisky Heroes profile, both fetched this session); produced under contract at Midleton since 1975. Neither page states a peat level for Paddy specifically; none is kept per the well-established convention that Midleton's mainline blends (Jameson, Powers, Paddy) use unpeated malt.

Resolved (seed found nothing): owned by Quality Spirits International, a William Grant & Sons subsidiary, since 1994; blended/bottled at Bellshill. Vatting of Speyside and Highland malts with Lowland grain, no peat mentioned -- kept none as a verified ordinary blend. "Skottish Collie" misspelling alias from the seed retained.

Resolved: William Pitters International (Bordeaux, founded 1964 by Bernard Magrez; now part of Marie Brizard Wine & Spirits) is the bottler -- sister brand to William Peel (already a live producer) under the same French owner, though a genuinely Scotch-legal product (blended/bottled in Scotland). No peat mentioned anywhere found; kept none per ordinary blend convention.

Confirmed: founded 1857 Edinburgh by J&W Hardie; blend acquired by Tomatin (owned by Takara Shuzo) with the J&W Hardie firm in 1996/97. Flag for reviewer: scotchwhisky.com's Whiskypedia entry says "a dash of Islay malt accounts for its light smokiness", but Tomatin's own current site (2024 relaunch, three cask-finish expressions) states only "the finest Highland and Speyside malts with Lowland grains" and does not mention Islay or smoke at all -- trusted the producer's own, more current statement and kept none rather than asserting the withheld light-peat claim from the older trade source, since that source isn't Tomatin's own domain and conflicts with Tomatin's current copy.

Resolved (seed found nothing): official site (bagotswhiskey.com) confirms Irish whiskey; Core Collection spans Grain Game (grain), Triple Batch (grain+malt blend) and a Single Malt (100% malted barley) -- defaultTypeName stays empty, kind changed blend->brand since the range isn't a single "blend" product. No producer/distillery named on the site (may source from a contract distillery, as is common in Ireland). No peat mentioned; kept unknown rather than none given the single malt line's status is unconfirmed.

Confirmed via The Whisky Shop and a second retailer (Bondston), both fetched this session: Black Bull is Duncan Taylor's own Blended Scotch Whisky brand. Core range (Black Bull, Kyloe, Kyloe Sherry Finish) reads unpeated -- kept none. The catalogue's "Black Bull Peated Finish" sample is real (Duncan Taylor also sells a "Kyloe Peated"/"Peated Edition" SKU, both retailers independently describe it as heavily peated -- "very heavily peated", "a big blast of dry smoke"), but Duncan Taylor's own site (duncantaylor.com) is JS-rendered and returned no extractable text across three attempts this session, so withheld peat proposal: heavy, per whiskyshop.com/black-bull-peated-edition and bondston.com/black-bull-peated-p13853 -- no rule.tsv row added since neither citation is the producer's own domain and Duncan Taylor is not Islay-based; flag for a reviewer who can browse duncantaylor.com/en-GB/kyloe-peated directly.

Resolved (seed found nothing): Carpathian is Romania's first single malt whisky, produced at Alexandrion Saber 1789 Distilleries (Alexandrion Group) along the Carpathian Mountains; master distiller Allan Anderson. Corrected kind blend->distillery is NOT applied here since this is a bottler/estate brand of the Alexandrion group rather than a single named distillery site in sources found -- kept kind=blend per input but flagged: every product found is single malt, various cask finishes (Shiraz, Palo Cortado, Madeira, Bourbon, Port). Official range page: a distinct, separately-marketed "medium peated" collection uses Belgian malt smoked with Scottish peat -- baseline (including this batch's Shiraz/Palo Cortado samples) kept none, with a "peated" pattern rule added for any SKU naming it (see rule.tsv), corroborated on the producer's own domain.

Resolved the seed's own flag: scotchwhisky.com's Inver House Distillers page (re-fetched this session) explicitly lists "Catto's Blended Scotch Whisky" among Inver House's brands (created by James Catto, Aberdeen, 1861; head office Airdrie; Inver House owned by International Beverage Holdings/ThaiBev since 2001/2006) -- ownership now directly confirmed rather than "trade knowledge". peatProfile=none kept as a category default for an ordinary blend; no Catto's-specific peat statement found.

Resolved the seed's own flag: Wikipedia (re-fetched this session) confirms William Grant & Sons owns Clan MacGregor, listed among their blended Scotch brands alongside Grant's and The Famous Grouse. Blend of 15 malt and grain whiskies; no peat statement found, inferred unpeated from the input's own totalwine.com tasting-note citation ("delicate sweet, smooth mellow", no smoke) -- kept none.
